title: Prayer breakfasts and Doug Coe

tellings.quote: I think they had prayer breakfasts and that kind of thing. They they get together and they talk about >> Doug Co.
this guy Doug Coe was the one of the leaders of the family in the '80s, and he would hold this prayer breakfast, and all of the presidents would have to attend the prayer breakfast
tellings.difference: Puts it in the 1980s and says every president had to attend.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell of Doug Coe, a leader of the Family, holding prayer breakfasts in Washington.

plain: A man named Doug Coe is said to have led a powerful religious group in Washington that Michels calls the Family, and to have hosted prayer breakfasts that every president had to attend. Peter Levenda, a researcher and writer, tells Michels that the group held prayer breakfasts and gatherings, and Coe's name comes up as he speaks. Michels, on a later episode and without naming a source, says Coe was one of the Family's leaders in the 1980s and that all the presidents had to come to his prayer breakfast. If true, it would mean a private religious circle had regular access to the highest levels of US power.
